subject: Re: Follow-up: Data access controls & support access (RBAC, break-glass)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Data access controls & support access (RBAC, break-glass)

Thanks again for taking the call this morning, Jared — really appreciate the context on FinTrust's upcoming LLM pilot. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Notes from the call:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood for document ingestion + redaction + customer-facing assistant (PII-sensitive).
- Key controls you asked about: RBAC/least-privilege for model access, support/engineer access patterns (including break-glass), audit logging for data access, and data residency/retention policies.

Clarifying questions we had (where your input will help us prioritize):
1) Scope of PII: will the pilot surface full SSNs/CCNs or primarily limited identifiers (emails, names, partial account numbers)?
2) Retention expectations: do you need ephemeral inference-only storage (no logs retained), 30/90/365 day retention windows, or a custom retention policy tied to compliance reviews?
3) Support access model: do you require formalized break-glass approvals + ticketing + time-limited keys for any support engagement?

What we can provide immediately (attached and linked):
- Redwood RBAC overview (high-level roles: org-admin, model-admin, app-deployer, support-operator) and how least-privilege is enforced through policy bundles (attached: redwood-rbac-overview.pdf).
- SOC 2 Type II summary and auditor contact (attached: SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf).
- Break-glass playbook template we use with enterprise customers (attached: break-glass-playbook.docx).

Proposed next steps:
- Tech deep-dive with your security/infra team and our security SE (Neha) — 60 min — can we do next Wed (9/29) or Thu (9/30)?
- Meanwhile, if you can confirm the PII scope and preferred retention window, Neha will prepare a short design showing RBAC mappings, support access flow, and audit-log retention options.

Happy to coordinate times. Thanks —

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jared Lawson <jared.lawson@fintrust.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@fintrust.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data access controls & support access (RBAC, break-glass)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few quick clarifications from our side:

PII scope: for the pilot we'll be ingesting KYC docs and transaction descriptions. Expect names, emails, dates of birth, and occasionally full account numbers. We will NOT be sending SSNs in the pilot, but eventual production could include those.

Retention: default requirement is 90 days for processed inference logs, but security is asking if we can configure per-environment retention (pilot = 30 days, prod = 365) and get the ability to purge on demand.

Support access: yes, we require documented break-glass procedures. Support must request via ticketing system (we use ServiceNow), get approval from an on-call security approver, and access should be time-bound and logged. We also need role separation so support cannot change retention policies.

A couple more asks:
- Can you confirm whether audit logs include token-level identifiers (i.e., which API key made the call) and whether those logs can be exported to our SIEM (we use Splunk)?
- Any options for ensuring data never leaves our chosen region (us-east-1)?

If Neha can cover the RBAC mappings and the break-glass flow in the deep-dive that would be ideal. Thurs 9/30 after 11am PT works for us.

Thanks —
Jared
Lead Product Security Engineer, FinTrust

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Lawson <jared.lawson@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data access controls & support access (RBAC, break-glass)

Hi Jared,

Thanks for the details — super helpful. Quick technical responses to your asks and what we'll cover in the deep-dive:

1) RBAC & least privilege:
- We provide fine-grained roles and policy bundles that map to org-level and environment-level scopes. Example roles: org-admin (full), env-admin (per-environment), model-reader, model-infer (tokenized access), support-operator (diagnostic only).
- Policies can be scoped to resource labels (project, environment, model-version) so you can grant model-infer but prevent modification of retention settings.

2) Break-glass & support access:
- We support time-limited support keys (one-time-use or TTL-based) and an audit-triggered automated notification to owners.
- Our recommended flow: support raises ticket -> on-call security approves (ServiceNow webhook) -> Redwood issues time-limited scoped key tied to the ticket id -> key is logged and exported to your SIEM.
- We also support just-in-time privileged access integrations (Okta SNC) for seamless approval flows.

3) Audit logs & exports:
- Audit logs capture API key, caller identity (OIDC subject), timestamp, operation type, model id, and truncated request metadata (we can redact request bodies for PII).
- Logs are exportable via secure push (TLS) to Splunk/CloudWatch/Datadog or pulled via an S3 export bucket. We can also stream to your SIEM over a private endpoint.

4) Data residency & retention:
- Hosted deployments can be pinned to a region (us-east-1). For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment (VPC) so data and keys never leave your network boundary.
- Retention is configurable per-environment; you can set retention windows (0/30/90/365) and trigger on-demand purges via authenticated admin APIs (we log purge actions for audit).

Attachments we can share during the deep-dive: redwood-rbac-overview.pdf (roles/policy examples), break-glass-playbook.docx (example approval flow), SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf.

I'll prepare an RBAC mapping template for FinTrust (env: pilot/prod) and walk through the break-glass sequence during the session.

One note on PII handling: for inference-only pipelines we can enable request-body redaction in logs and store only metadata. If you need full request retention for debugging we recommend an isolated debug environment with tighter retention and access controls.

I'll plan to demo the ticket->key flow and log export to Splunk in the session. See you on Thu 9/30 after 11am PT.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
